uranyl_ions_per_pore.note: conclusion is essentially one uranyl ion per pore; with integer school-book atomic masses the value is 1.020 -> 1.02 at 3 s.f.

assumptions: Tabulated relative atomic masses are not printed in the problem materials; CODATA 2022 standard values used (C 12.011, H 1.008, N 14.007, O 15.999, U 238.02891) as trusted general-law constants. Result robust: 1.00 (CODATA) vs 1.02 (integer school-book masses) at 3 s.f.

A 'pore' is one hexagonal opening of the honeycomb (hcb) layer; one pore corresponds to one two-vertex cell of framework with COF-9 repeat formula C36H27N9O3 (= E1 + D2 - 3 H2O + 3 NH3O), derived from the printed Q3-6/Q3-7 structures. One pore per two vertices follows from Euler's formula for any 3-connected periodic net (proved/justified in answer.md).
Avogadro constant cancels exactly; the Lean proof quantifies over arbitrary NA ≠ 0.
source_gaps: No atomic-mass table or Avogadro constant is printed anywhere in the supplied Q3 materials; Output 2 numerically depends on these standard external constants. The problem itself only asks to 'indicate' the number per pore, which is 1.00 (essentially one) under either standard mass table.
